name: McKinsey & Company
hq: New York, United States (no formal global HQ)
paris: Main French office at 35-37 boulevard des Invalides (Paris 7e), with a smaller Lyon office; ~700 consultants in France (2025, down from ~800 in 2023), led by Clarisse Magnin, covering all major sector and functional practices incl. energy, automotive, consumer and sustainability.
employees: ~40,000 worldwide (Jan 2026), plus ~20,000 AI agents per the CEO; ~700 consultants in France (2025)
revenue: Not disclosed; roughly $15-16bn annually, flat for ~5 years (Dec 2025 estimate reported via Bloomberg/Storyboard18)
description: The world's best-known strategy consultancy, advising CEOs, governments and institutions on strategy, operations, organisation, digital/AI and sustainability. Highly generalist with deep industry practices, a large research arm (McKinsey Global Institute) and AI unit QuantumBlack.
sectors: Generalist: energy & materials, automotive & assembly, consumer & retail (incl. luxury), financial services, healthcare, TMT, public sector; strong sustainability and AI practices
health: Revenue has plateaued (~$15-16bn) and headcount fell from ~45,000 (2022) to ~40,000; the French partnership shrank from 71 to 59 partners (2024-25) and further support-function cuts were reported in Dec 2025. The firm is pushing hard into AI (20,000 agents) and will elect a new global managing partner in 2027.

news.title: McKinsey senior partners to meet in Sydney to elect next global managing partner (2027)

McKinsey adds AI (Lilli) exercise to final-round interviews; counts 20,000 AI agents

recruiting: Interns (stage of 2-6 months) and Business Analysts (graduates) apply online year-round; the process is the McKinsey Solve online game, then a first round of two interviews (case + personal experience interview) and a final round of 2-3 with partners, which now includes an AI-assisted exercise using the internal tool Lilli. Very selective (top Grandes Écoles), working French required and interviews often mix French and English.
tinoAngle: His Singapore internship and multi-country exposure fit McKinsey's global staffing, and his industrial ash-recovery project maps directly onto its Sustainability and Energy & Materials practices; the Paris office's automotive and consumer work matches his sector interests.

name: Boston Consulting Group (BCG)
paris: Large Paris office on avenue de la Grande Armée (16e), led by Olivier Scalabre, historically hiring ~70-90 people a year; BCG France posted record revenue of ~€645m in 2025 (Consultor headline).
employees: ~33,500 worldwide (2025); France headcount not disclosed (Paris office ~1,000 consultants per older Consultor profile)
description: Global strategy consultancy founded by Bruce Henderson, known for the growth-share matrix and today for large transformations and tech/AI work through BCG X. Over 40% of revenue now comes from AI- and tech-related services.
sectors: Generalist: energy, automotive & mobility, consumer & luxury, industrial goods, financial institutions, health, TMT, public sector; strong Climate & Sustainability and BCG X (AI/tech)
health: Strong: 22nd consecutive year of growth in 2025 ($14.4bn, +7%), AI services +25%, headcount up to 33,500, and BCG overtook McKinsey on headcount. In 2026 it launched an interim-management offer (first in Germany and France).

BCG launches interim-management offer, starting in Germany and France

recruiting: Interns join as Visiting Associates (typically 6-month stages) and graduates as Associates; after CV screening, Paris candidates usually take an online aptitude test (a cognitive test reported since 2024; Casey/Pymetrics in some offices) followed by interview rounds of two case + fit interviews each (historically three rounds in Paris). Top school profiles expected; French and English both needed.
tinoAngle: BCG's Climate & Sustainability practice and its energy and automotive work in Paris fit his CSR ash-valorisation project and sector interests, while his Singapore internship is a credible link to BCG's large Southeast Asia system.

name: Bain & Company
paris: Paris office at 25 avenue Kléber (16e) with ~49 partners (2025), leader in French private-equity due diligence and strong in consumer/retail, energy & utilities, TMT and a fast-growing enterprise technology practice.
employees: 18,000+ worldwide (2022 figure; ~12,000 client-facing staff in 2026); France headcount not disclosed
description: Strategy consultancy founded by former BCG partners, known for results-oriented work, the Net Promoter System and the world's leading private-equity consulting practice. Publishes the reference luxury market study with Altagamma.
sectors: Private equity, consumer products & retail, luxury, energy & natural resources, utilities, TMT, financial services, healthcare; growing AI/tech practice
health: Growing: CEO Christophe De Vusser said in Sep 2026 that AI demand drives double-digit revenue growth and that consulting headcount will rise ~12% (~1,400 hires) in 2026, with graduate intake up >10% in 2026 and 2027 and no layoffs planned.

Bain report: AI now at the top of the agenda for luxury houses
Bain invests in the new OpenAI Deployment Company

recruiting: Interns are Associate Consultant Interns (ACI) and graduates Associate Consultants (AC). Process: Gorilla online test (numerical, logic, business sense, written English), then round 1 (one case + one behavioural interview) and round 2 (one case for ACI, two for AC, plus a motivation interview). English is assessed explicitly; French expected in Paris.
tinoAngle: Bain is the reference firm for luxury (Bain-Altagamma study) and has an active energy & utilities practice in Paris, matching two of his target sectors; his sales internship in Madrid and Singapore experience support its client-results, commercial culture.

name: Roland Berger
paris: Paris office (open since 1990-91) with 41 partners as of Feb 2026, led by Laurent Benarousse with a six-person leadership team (May 2026); notable public-sector, consumer, operations and energy/climate/circular-economy work.
employees: ~3,500 worldwide across 52 offices (2025-26); France headcount not disclosed (~300 staff in 2021)
ownership: Independent, owned solely by its partners
description: The only top-tier strategy consultancy of European (German) origin, strong in industrial sectors, restructuring and transformation. Known for automotive, industrial and restructuring expertise and an engineering-minded client base.
sectors: Automotive (historic flagship), industrials, energy & utilities, aerospace & defence, consumer goods & retail, healthcare, public sector, restructuring; sustainability/circular economy
health: Record €1.01bn revenue in 2025 with growth in all regions (Asia +19%, Americas +11%), new Houston and Sydney offices, and partner growth in Paris (35 to 41). Management warned 2026 would be more challenging and is focusing on profitability.

news.title: Roland Berger: one in four new cars sold globally is now electric

recruiting: Paris hires 'Stagiaire Consultant' interns (6-12 month gap-year or end-of-studies stages; 2027 postings already open) and Junior Consultants. Typical process: CV + cover letter, round 1 (group case or two short interviews), round 2 (two one-hour case + fit interviews), plus a third round for permanent hires; fluent French and English mandatory, a third language a plus, and at least 6 months of prior experience expected.
tinoAngle: Roland Berger's automotive heritage and Paris energy/climate/circular-economy team (led by Claire Pernet) match his automotive interest and industrial waste-valorisation project; his Spanish and logistics background fit its operations and supply-chain work, and it posts 2027 intern roles fitting his Jan-Jul 2027 window.

name: Kearney
paris: Paris office led by Kearney France president Jérôme Souied; it has been shrinking sharply, with 15 partner departures since Dec 2023 and an internal source citing fewer than 100 consultants in 2026 (vs 150-200 in 2025), mostly staffed on international projects.
employees: ~5,700 worldwide (2026); Paris <100 consultants per internal source (Mar 2026)
ownership: Private partnership (partner-owned since 2006 buy-back from EDS)
description: Global management consultancy marking its centenary in 2026, best known for operations, procurement and supply-chain strategy alongside corporate strategy and its FDI Confidence Index. Partners each hold an equal governance vote.
sectors: Procurement, operations & supply chain, consumer & retail, automotive, energy, industrials, telecoms, financial services, public sector (strong in Middle East)
health: Globally stable and investing (new CFO Sep 2026, AI procurement tool with Beroe, Middle East expansion), but the Paris office is in deep difficulty: its consumer/retail practice left for Oliver Wyman and Consultor (Mar 2026) describes the worst crisis in its Paris history.

news.title: Kearney appoints Martin Denman as chief financial officer

recruiting: Entry roles are interns and Business Analysts; process is CV screening (school, experience, languages), an online cognitive test (numerical, inductive, deductive), then case interviews: three for an internship, four over two rounds for a permanent role, sometimes in a one-day 'Recruiting Day' format with same-day answer. Fluent English needed given heavy international staffing.
tinoAngle: Kearney's operations, procurement and supply-chain DNA fits his import/export logistics internship and Singapore experience (strong Asia-Pacific presence); given the Paris turmoil, he should check current Paris openings or consider international offices.

name: Oliver Wyman
paris: Paris office at 1 rue Euler (8e) with ~225 consultants and ~40 partners (2025), historically strongest in financial services, plus telecoms/media, transport and consumer goods (reinforced by four ex-Kearney consumer/retail partners).
employees: Not disclosed separately; Marsh Management Consulting (Oliver Wyman, Lippincott, NERA) has 7,200+ staff (2025); ~225 consultants in Paris (2025)
ownership: Subsidiary of Marsh (formerly Marsh McLennan; NYSE: MRSH)
description: Global strategy and management consultancy owned by insurance broker Marsh, renowned for financial services and risk, and also active in transport, aviation, consumer, energy and public sector. Combines strategy work with deep analytics and actuarial expertise.
sectors: Financial services & risk (flagship), transportation & aviation, automotive, consumer & retail, energy & utilities, health & life sciences, telecoms, public sector; restructuring (CR3)
health: Healthy: record $3.6bn revenue in 2025 (+6%), first $1bn quarter, similar growth expected in 2026; new CEO Ted Moynihan (Apr 2026) and acquisition of turnaround firm CR3 Partners (May 2026). Management said it plans to hire as many or more junior consultants who are comfortable with AI.

recruiting: Paris hires interns and Consultants (graduate entry). Interns go through 2 rounds (1 then 2 case + fit interviews); graduate Consultants through 3 rounds (1, 2, then 1 interview). Candidates usually choose a practice affiliation; French and English expected.
tinoAngle: Oliver Wyman's transport/automotive and newly reinforced consumer & retail practice in Paris fit his sector interests, and its large Singapore/Asia business and energy work connect with his international and industrial-sustainability experience.

name: Arthur D. Little
paris: Paris office at 7 place d'Iéna (16e) with 100+ consultants and ~16 partners in France (2025), led by Matteo Ainardi (Western Europe & France/Morocco), strong in telecoms, transport, consumer/luxury, automotive, energy and private equity (25-30% of activity).
employees: 2,000+ worldwide in ~40 offices (2026); 100+ consultants in France (2025)

sectors: Telecoms/TIME, transport & airports, automotive & mobility, energy & utilities, consumer & luxury, chemicals/process industries, life sciences, private equity
health: Stable and expanding selectively: new partners in Paris and Madrid (Apr 2026), Middle East and Tokyo promotions, a joint venture with Vega IT (Dec 2025), and a push to grow US revenue from $38m (2025) to ~$45m (2026).

tinoAngle: ADL Paris explicitly covers luxury/consumer, automotive and energy-environment, all three of his target sectors, and its technology-and-innovation angle suits his industrial ash-recovery project; its Madrid and Middle East/Asia footprint value his Spanish and Singapore experience.

hq: London, United Kingdom (large hub in Boston)
paris: Paris office (since 1989) at 2 rue Paul Cézanne (8e) with ~14 partners and ~100 consultants (2026), led by Anne Dhulesia; core in private equity/M&A, life sciences, industry-energy-construction, consumer, retail and tech.
employees: 2,300+ worldwide in 25+ offices (2025-26); ~100 consultants in Paris (2026)

recruiting: Entry titles are Analyst / Associate (and interns). Process: online numerical test in English, round 1 with two consultant interviews (market-sizing or strategy case + fit, one fully in English), round 2 with two partner case + fit interviews. Analytical rigour is weighted heavily.
tinoAngle: L.E.K.'s industry-energy practice and PE due-diligence work suit an analytical, industrial profile like his waste-valorisation project, and its Singapore office plus new Spain/LatAm push make use of his Asian experience and Spanish.

name: Strategy& (PwC)
hq: London, United Kingdom (PwC network); Paris team in Neuilly-sur-Seine
paris: Around 200 consultants in Paris (Consultor) based at PwC's Neuilly-sur-Seine campus, with 22 partners in France after the 2023 promotions; led since July 2026 by Laurent Guérin.

revenue: PwC: $56.9bn (FY2025, year to June 2025); Strategy& not disclosed separately
description: PwC's global strategy consulting brand, created when Booz & Company joined PwC in 2014. It combines classic strategy work with PwC's deals, operations and tech capabilities, positioning itself on 'strategy through execution'. Strong in M&A-related strategy (carve-outs, spin-offs, post-merger integration) and private equity value creation.
sectors: Energy & utilities, consumer goods & retail, aerospace & defence, TMT, financial services, private equity; also restructuring, operations and decarbonisation
health: PwC grew only 2.7% in FY2025 and cut headcount 1.6%, but Strategy& is investing: it bought UK AI consultancy Datasparq (Aug 2026) and PwC Australia acquired Advancy Australia (Sept 2026). France saw a leadership change in July 2026; Paris was still posting junior roles in May 2026.

recruiting: Entry titles are intern/apprentice and Associate (junior consultant). Interns go through 4 interviews and graduates 5, each mixing fit and case study, conducted in both French and English (Consultor). Looks for top business/engineering school profiles with strong analytics and sector curiosity.
tinoAngle: Energy is one of Strategy&'s core French sectors and its operations practice covers decarbonisation and circular economy, a direct link to Tino's industrial waste/ash valorisation project; his Singapore internship fits PwC's global network and international staffing.

name: EY-Parthenon
hq: London, United Kingdom (EY global); Parthenon originally Boston, USA
paris: In France about 650 consultants and 80 partners (2025), of which 200+ in Strategy & Transformation; Paris strategy teams sit at rue Saint-Lazare (9th) and move to One Monceau (8th) in 2026, with new regional offices in Bordeaux and Toulouse.
revenue: EY: $57.0bn (FY2026, to June 2026); Strategy and Transactions (EY-Parthenon): $6.8bn (FY2026)
description: EY's strategy and transactions brand, combining Parthenon's strategy consulting heritage with EY's transaction and corporate finance teams. In France it was built largely from the 2017 absorption of OC&C's Paris office and covers growth strategy, performance, due diligence, carve-outs and post-merger integration. About a third of missions involve other EY lines (consulting, law, sustainability).
sectors: Industry & mobility (automotive), retail & consumer goods, TMT; also financial services, public sector, health, education and energy
health: Strong: EY's Strategy and Transactions line grew 7.4% in local currency to $6.8bn in FY2026, faster than EY overall (4.7%). France has grown about 10% a year since 2017 and kept expanding in 2026 (Toulouse office, larger Paris premises).

recruiting: Entry titles are intern, Associate Consultant and Senior Associate. Process has 3 rounds: a quantitative test plus one case, then two cases, then a final case (Consultor). French and English are expected; separate tracks exist for strategy and for transaction work (PMI/carve-out, due diligence).
tinoAngle: Industry & mobility is a lead French sector, matching Tino's automotive interest, and the integrated model with EY sustainability teams suits his CSR waste-valorisation project; his import/export logistics internship is relevant for supply-chain and carve-out work.

name: Accenture Strategy
paris: Accenture's Strategy & Consulting teams in France count about 1,500 people out of ~10,000 Accenture staff in the country (Jan 2025), including a ~100-person Technology Strategy team; strategy work covers M&A, strategic plans and large transformations.
employees: About 814,000 people globally (Oct 2026, Q4 FY2026 release); ~779,000 at Aug 2025
revenue: Accenture: $74.2bn (FY2026, to Aug 2026), of which Consulting $36.9bn; Strategy not disclosed separately
description: Strategy unit of Accenture's Strategy & Consulting business, merged organisationally with consulting since 2020. Positions itself on business strategy tied to technology and AI, with the ability to carry recommendations into implementation through the wider group.
sectors: Organised by industry matrix incl. automotive, industrial/manufacturing, utilities & energy, retail & consumer goods, aviation, financial services; plus functional practices (finance, HR, technology strategy)
health: Mixed: FY2026 revenue grew 6% to $74.2bn, but Accenture ran an ~$865m restructuring in late 2025 (11,000+ cuts in one quarter) and keeps buying AI/data firms in Europe. In France, Consultor reported pay freezes, low staffing and morale issues in 2024-25.

tinoAngle: Accenture's automotive and utilities/energy industry groups line up with Tino's target sectors, and its large international network suits his Singapore and Madrid experience; Spanish is a plus for Iberian projects.

health: Stable and growing in Europe: it rehired a 35-person team and partners from EY-Parthenon in Germany (2024-25) and kept promoting partners in 2025-26. No public Paris headcount update since 2022.
